research_mode: official Home Office sources only; monthly validation, offence and outcome rule checks, record-level versus aggregate supply and Crimsec4 time semantics; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Obsolete offence-classification validation
verified_claims: monthly validation checks for data supplied against offence classifications that no longer exist
former fraud classifications are given as an example
the check is performed before publication
limitations: classification validity does not establish correct local recording
reference lists remain edition-dependent

sources.name: Long-term trend outlier validation
verified_claims: offence and outcome types are compared with long-term trends
the purpose is to identify outliers in monthly data
identified anomalies are returned to forces for investigation
limitations: trend conformity is not proof of correctness
structural changes can create legitimate outliers

sources.name: Rape-caution validation query
verified_claims: monthly checks identify cautions assigned to rape offences
outcomes 2 and 3 are included in this check
cases are queried with Force Crime Registrars
limitations: a query is a validation action rather than proof of error
case-level resolution is not published in the aggregate annex

sources.name: Outcome 17 time-limit rule check
verified_claims: Home Office validation checks outcome 17 applications
the check looks for outcome 17 applied to offences without a time limit
incompatible applications are queried
limitations: validation rules depend on the current outcomes framework
aggregate checks do not replace force record review

sources.name: Outcome 7 offence-scope rule check
verified_claims: Home Office validation checks outcome 7 applications
outcome 7 is checked against cannabis or khat offence scope
applications to other offences are queried
limitations: the rule is framework-specific
a valid code combination is not a measure of local safety

sources.name: Anomaly explanation and resubmission process
verified_claims: forces are asked to investigate identified anomalies
forces can provide an explanation when the value is valid
forces resubmit figures when an error has occurred
limitations: force response is part of production QA rather than independent inspection
later revisions remain possible

sources.name: Home Office Data Hub record-level supply
verified_claims: the Home Office Data Hub accepts record-level offence detail
record-level supply substantially expands analysis opportunities
the data source differs from aggregate Crimsec4 returns
limitations: record-level Home Office data are not public parcel records
analysis opportunity does not guarantee uniform force fields

sources.name: Residual aggregate Crimsec4 supply
verified_claims: a small number of forces supply crime and outcome data through an aggregate return
the return is the Crimsec4 form
the form is supplied monthly
limitations: aggregate-return forces have less analytical detail than record-level submissions
coverage can change by edition

sources.name: Crimsec4 notifiable-offence scope
verified_claims: Crimsec4 collects data for crimes on the notifiable offence list
notifiable offences include offences that could be tried by jury
the list also includes specified closely related summary offences
limitations: notifiable scope is broader than only serious jury trials
the list is not equivalent to all incidents known to police

sources.name: Crimsec4 outcome-month semantics
verified_claims: Crimsec4 records an outcome in the month the outcome is applied
the month can differ from the month or year of the original offence
an offence in January charged in June is recorded as a June outcome
limitations: monthly offence and outcome volumes are not matched cohorts
timeliness requires record-level or cohort-aware analysis
